summary: You've got drive and discipline pulling the same direction. You can work hard for a long time without burning out, the rare kind of stamina that finishes what it starts. Controlled, sustained effort is your natural gear.
body: You've got drive and discipline pulling the same direction. You can work hard for a long time without burning out, the rare kind of stamina that finishes what it starts. Controlled, sustained effort is your natural gear. While other people sprint and crash, you pace. The only risk in something this reliable is taking it for granted, assuming the engine will always be there and never pushing it. Point it at something worthy and you'll out-build everyone in the room.
gift: At your best: disciplined, durable, the one who actually finishes.
shadow: The trap: coasting on reliable stamina and never aiming it at anything big.
integration: Let drive and anger and discipline and limits cooperate without making either one carry the whole story. Endurance and discipline; the friction is the constant start-stop of push against restraint.
do: Aim the stamina at something worth finishing
Pace the long effort on purpose
Push the engine before you assume it's there
